rationales: Gas molecules move freely rather than staying in fixed positions.
Liquid molecules can move past one another.
In a solid, molecules vibrate about fixed positions and do not leave them.
Plasma particles move freely, so they do not stay in fixed positions.

Vi − Vf = at has the velocity difference in the wrong order.
The squared-velocity equation is Vf² − Vi² = 2as, not a²t².
This is not a correct equation of motion.
The digit 3 is significant, so the count is not zero.
Leading zeros are not significant, so 0.03 has one significant figure.
The leading zeros do not count; only the 3 is significant.
0.03 contains one significant figure, not three.
Ns is not equivalent to the force unit newton.
kg m s⁻¹ is the unit of momentum, not force.

N s⁻¹ is not a unit of force.

6.67 is the approximate value of the universal gravitational constant in different units, not Earth’s field strength.

Earth’s gravitational field strength is approximately 9.8 N kg⁻¹, not 8.9 N kg⁻¹.
The body’s height does not determine its kinetic energy, and it is stated to be placed on the table.
At rest, the body has no kinetic energy, so it is not 20 J.
The body has gravitational potential energy, but that is not kinetic energy.
A body placed on the table is at rest, so its kinetic energy is zero.
A curved force–extension graph does not show the proportional relationship required by Hooke’s law.
A straight line through the origin represents force proportional to extension and obeys Hooke’s law.
A straight rising line that does not pass through the origin would not show direct proportionality, so its description does not establish that it obeys Hooke’s law.
A horizontal line does not show force proportional to extension and does not obey Hooke’s law; thus more than one described graph fails the law, making the question ambiguous.

0°F is below water’s freezing point.
